text:
The least likely to follow from Savigny's Volksgeist is the claim in your note: that a people's spirit is too uniform and abstract to shape particular legal rules, so law is only loosely and incidentally tied to culture. Savigny held the opposite. Law grows organically out of a specific people's history, customs and shared convictions, so its content is closely bound to national character. That is also why he opposed imposing a universal code, as in the Thibaut debate.

I still don't have the original answer options, so this is a judgment about your note's claim, not a choice from a list.

CONFIDENCE: 72
